tools.name: check_drug_approval_fda_eu
tools.description: Answers whether a drug or medicine is approved, authorised, licensed or registered in a country or in the EU (for example, whether it is FDA approved in the US), or approved there for a condition, today or on a past date, and which official record settles that. Records are held for the US (the FDA's approval record on Drugs@FDA for whether a medicine is approved, and the prescribing information on DailyMed, as submitted to the FDA, for what it is approved for) and, for centrally authorised medicines, for the EU and EEA (the European Commission's product information), and for the authorised medicines of Brazil, Canada, Colombia, Czechia, Denmark, France, Italy, Latvia, the Netherlands, Poland, Slovakia, Switzerland, Taiwan and the United Kingdom (each country's own competent-authority register), and each answer resting on one carries its pointer URL. For any other market, the answer names that market's competent authority and where its registration record is published, each where it is identified, and says which is not. Where the authority's own record of the medicine is read, it settles registration (P1); the coverage field states, for the claim asked, whether the authority was identified, its record examined and the claim verified, so registration and indication are never read as one.Otherwise the claim is unresolved, or supported, never settled, by the authorisation holder's own label, and the answer carries a referral to the authority's own register or product information: a route to verification, not evidence. For one medicine, one market and one date, the answer gives which source settles whether the medicine is registered (P1) or authorised for an indication (P2), what that source says about the claim where its content has been checked, where this market's label differs from the US and EU labels, and what is unresolved. supported_attested means the authorisation holder's own approved label, read under the attestation conditions, states the claim; it never settles it. Where that label does not state the indication, or its content has not been checked, the answer is unresolved. An unresolved answer means AlphaCitation cannot currently verify the claim from a held record; it is not evidence about the medicine's status. Every answer that does not settle carries abstention, one reason code (insufficient_evidence, authority_inaccessible, conflicting_records, stale_evidence, unsupported_claim_type, snapshot_only) with its meaning.

tools.name: read_drug_label_fda_eu
tools.description: Answers what a drug's or medicine's official FDA label (the US prescribing information) or EU summary of product characteristics (SmPC) says, and its FDA approval or EU authorisation facts, today or on a past date: what it is approved or authorised for and in whom, dosage, contraindications, the boxed warning, warnings and precautions, use in pregnancy, breastfeeding, children and older people, adverse reactions, interactions, overdose, pharmacology, storage, and the label's version history. For the US it reads the application holder's label as published on DailyMed and the FDA's approval record on Drugs@FDA; for the EU it reads each SmPC in the European Commission's product information as published by the EMA, and the EMA's medicines data. Each answer gives the record's own words for the section asked, with the section number, the document's version, its effective date, the SHA-256 of the exact document read and its address, and the source to acknowledge. Where a product information holds several SmPCs (strengths or forms), each is given apart. The indications text is the record's statement; whether a particular use falls within it is not decided, except for an indication from the published list, where the reference lookup's own answer is given beside it. Where the record cannot be read, matched or confirmed for the date, no text is given: the answer is unresolved, with one reason code (insufficient_evidence, authority_inaccessible, conflicting_records, stale_evidence, unsupported_claim_type, snapshot_only) and its meaning.

medicine.description: The brand or active substance name, exactly (for example Jardiance or empagliflozin).

topic.description: What to read. approval: whether and since when it is approved or authorised, its current status, application or product number and holder; indications: what it is approved or authorised for, and in whom (US section 1; SmPC 4.1); dosage: dose and how it is given (US section 2; SmPC 4.2); dosage_forms: dosage forms and strengths (US section 3; SmPC 2 and 3); contraindications: contraindications (US section 4; SmPC 4.3); boxed_warning: the boxed warning (US only; the SmPC has none); warnings_precautions: warnings and precautions (US section 5; SmPC 4.4); adverse_reactions: adverse reactions (US section 6; SmPC 4.8); interactions: interactions (US section 7; SmPC 4.5); specific_populations: use in specific populations (US section 8; SmPC 4.6, with 4.2 for the paediatric and elderly populations); pregnancy: pregnancy (US 8.1; SmPC 4.6); lactation: lactation and breastfeeding (US 8.2; SmPC 4.6); pediatric: use in children (US 8.4; SmPC 4.1 and 4.2); geriatric: use in older people (US 8.5; SmPC 4.2); overdose: overdose (US section 10; SmPC 4.9); pharmacodynamics: mechanism of action and pharmacodynamics (US 12.1 and 12.2; SmPC 5.1); pharmacokinetics: pharmacokinetics (US 12.3; SmPC 5.2); pharmaceutical_particulars: storage, shelf life, excipients and container (US section 16; SmPC 6.1 to 6.6); history: the label's published versions and dates, and what changed in a section between two versions where both are published.

date.description: The date the question is about, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today (UTC).

product.description: Optional: a strength or form as the label names it (for example 395 mg, or solution for injection), to choose among several SmPCs or labels.

application.description: Optional: the exact application, a US NDA, ANDA or BLA number (for example ANDA078071) or an EMA product number (for example EMEA/H/C/002677), so a generic or a duplicate authorisation is answered for itself.

indication.description: Optional, with topic indications: an indication from the published list, to add the reference lookup's own answer for it.

section.description: Optional, with topic history and since: the section whose change is shown.

since.description: Optional, with topic history and section: show what changed in the section between the version published on this date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the current one.

tools.name: lookup_precedent_ruling
tools.description: For one ruling identifier (ACPREC-YYYY-NNNN): what was decided about an evidence conflict, why, on which records, its status now (settled, unresolved or superseded) and its RFC 3161 timestamp where one has been issued, together with a fresh lookup of the current governing record for the ruling's medicine, market and date where the ruling names one. A ruling is not evidence and decides no claim today; the current governing record does, and the ruling records only how the earlier conflict was decided. Where no current record is held, the answer names the competent authority and where its own record is published.

id.description: The ruling identifier, for example ACPREC-2026-0001.

date.description: The date to resolve the current record for, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today (UTC).
